name: Srikanta Sivacarya
dates_notes: The date, intellectual setting, and relation of Śrīkaṇṭha to the Nīlakaṇṭha of later Vīraśaiva materials remain disputed; modern scholarship does not support a narrow secure date.
core_thesis: Śrīkaṇṭha Śivācārya is the author traditionally associated with the *Brahmamīmāṃsābhāṣya*, a Śaiva commentary on the *Brahma-sūtras* later called the *Śrīkaṇṭha-bhāṣya*. The commentary reads the Vedāntic Brahman as Śiva and gives Śakti a constitutive role in explaining manifestation. Its relation to Rāmānuja's theology, Vīraśaiva materials, and later Śivādvaita is a central scholarly question rather than a settled genealogy. The text matters because Appayya Dīkṣita made it the principal earlier authority for his sixteenth-century Śaiva Vedānta; this record does not treat that later reception as proof of every doctrine attributed to Śrīkaṇṭha.

engaged_works.title: Brahmamimamsa-bhasya
engaged_works.ascription_notes: The commentary is consistently transmitted under Śrīkaṇṭha's name, while the identity and historical profile of its author remain debated.
engaged_works.summary: A complete Śaiva reading of the *Brahma-sūtras*. It identifies the ultimate referent of Vedāntic scriptural language with Śiva and interprets the relation of the supreme, souls, and world through a Śaiva theological framework. Printed Sanskrit editions exist, but no verified local witness has been linked for passage-level use.
